patch.description: Platform-admin mutation on a single runner. The body carries either `action` alone, or an edit: `assigned_policy`, `labels`, or both. An edit carrying both applies both or neither. `action` moves the admin state: `cordon` to cordoned, `drain` to draining, `revoke` to revoked. Revoked is terminal; a revoked runner cannot transition back. `self_test` moves no state. It records a request for the runner to test its own sandbox. The host picks the request up on its next heartbeat and answers on a later one. The reply is the recorded request, never a verdict. A revoked runner refuses it with 409 `UZ-RUN-018`, since it will never heartbeat again. `assigned_policy` reassigns the runner's policy, and the host picks it up on its next heartbeat. Sending the same policy again changes nothing and records no event. A revoked runner refuses a policy with 400. `labels` replaces the runner's whole label set, the labels a fleet's required tags are matched against on the runner's next lease poll. The bounds and the refusal are the ones enrollment applies. A label given twice is stored once, in the order first given, an empty list clears every label, and a revoked runner's labels stay editable. The reply carries `labels` as stored whenever the request sent them.

get.description: Platform-admin read of a single runner's lease history, newest first. Each lease is joined to its Fleet event, so outcome and failure cause arrive in one round trip. Stripe-style keyset pagination — `starting_after` is a lease id from a previous page's `next_cursor`. Settled leases are retained for 30 days. The window is measured from settlement, not from acquisition. A lease acquired long ago and settled yesterday keeps its full window. A background sweep deletes them past that window. A lease still running or renewing is never swept. The per-lease activity records (`lease_acquired`, `lease_released`) are swept on the same 30-day window. Each record ages from when it occurred, not from its lease's settlement. A long run's opening record can therefore be pruned shortly before its lease row. The runner's lifecycle activity is kept at any age, so a long-lived runner's feed never empties. A lease whose runner died without reporting is marked expired once it passes the same window. It then keeps its own window, like any settled lease. The lifetime totals on `GET /v1/fleets/runners/{id}` are unaffected by any of this. They count transitions as they happen, not surviving rows. A long-lived runner's `leases_acquired` will therefore exceed what this endpoint returns.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: A lease id this runner holds; the page starts strictly after it. A lease id the runner does not hold is refused. So is one outside the `workspace_id` or `fleet` filters when those filters are set. The cursor names a position in the filtered stream, so it must belong to it. A cursor whose lease the retention sweep has since deleted is refused for the same reason — start again from the first page.

get.description: Returns models available to the tenant. Each item includes its provider, context limit, and usage fields. An empty library returns an empty array. A bounded keyset page ordered by normalized `model_id`, then normalized `provider`, then an opaque row identity. Every comparison runs under `COLLATE "C"`, so the order is byte-wise and stable across locales. Follow `next_cursor` to read the whole catalogue; a client that reads only the first page silently loses every model past it. The response is conditionally revalidated. Every answer carries an `ETag` over the exact bytes served, plus `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` and `Vary: Authorization`. Send the tag back as `If-None-Match` and a match answers `304` with no body and the same headers. `private` is what stops a shared proxy handing one tenant's response to another even though the payload is identical for every authorized caller.

The daemon brackets every run. `event_received` carries `event_id`, `actor`, `event_type` and `created_at` when a run's row is written. A person's message adds `message`, the text they typed. `event_complete` carries the terminal row as `GET …/events` lists it, without `fleet_id` and `workspace_id`. The completion adds `fleet_status` and `pending_approvals`. It also carries `final_reply`, the reply text, when that text is at most 64 KiB. Without it, read the event detail. `gate_opened` and `gate_resolved` carry `gate_id`, `event_id` and `pending_approvals`. `event_id` is null for a gate raised outside a run. A resolved gate adds `status` and `resolved_by`. The runner's frames ride the same stream: `chunk`, `tool_call_started`, `tool_call_progress` and `tool_call_completed`. Each tool frame carries `event_id` and `name`. Newer runners add `call_id`, which every frame of one call shares and no other call of the event reuses. message.description: What the fleet is asked to do.

once.description: Whether it retires after its first fire. Beta: this field may change shape before it is stable.

oneOf.description: Explicit instance overlay, omitted when the pinned recipe is inherited.

source.description:
Who made it: `api` for a person, `trigger` for the fleet's own
document, `fleet` for the fleet while it ran. Only a `fleet` schedule
can be changed by the fleet. Beta: this field may change shape before it is stable.

status.description: What the operator wants it to be doing.

sync.description:
How far agentsfleet has brought the external scheduler in line.

A schedule can save without registering. This field shows you that
state.

timezone.description: The zone that expression is read in.

Visibility.description:
Who reads a stored entry: its own fleet, or every fleet in the workspace
granted to read shared memory.

WaitingInvite.description: One invite waiting for the caller's address.

expires_at.description: When it stops being acceptable, epoch milliseconds.

id.description: The invite's identifier, which the accept route names.

WebhookUrl.description: Public manual-webhook address for one declared source.

WorkspaceAccount.description: The account a listed workspace belongs to.

owner_name.description:
What a person calls the account: its owner's display name, or the
account's own name when the owner has none.

WorkspaceMember.description:
One member of a workspace's account, as its thread names senders.

No address: every member of an account can read this list, and a name is
all a thread needs.

actor.description:
The actor their messages record, `steer:<subject>`: what a thread
row's `actor` equals when this member sent it.

display_name.description: Their name, `null` when the identity provider supplied none.

WorkspaceModel.description: A priced explicit selection owned by the workspace's billing account.

ref.description: Opaque registry reference, including an explicit platform default.

WorkspaceSummary.description: One workspace as the list shows it.

account.description: The account it belongs to, which is how a dashboard groups the list.

created_at.description: When it was created; the walk's sort key.

name.description:
Its name — `null` on rows older than naming, emitted either way for
the tenant module's null rule.

role.description: The caller's role in that account: `owner` or `member`.

WorkspacesResponse.description:
`GET /v1/tenants/me/workspaces` — one page of the workspaces across every
account the caller holds.

items.description: The rows on this page, oldest first.

next_cursor.description: Where the next page resumes, or `null` on the last page.

tenant_id.description:
The caller's own account — the authoritative resolution, carried so a
client can pin its local state to the right person. Items from accounts
the caller joined name theirs in `account`.

total.description:
Always `null`: the walk never counts, and the key stays because a
client may already branch on its presence.

BearerAuth.description: Obtain a token via the CLI auth flow (POST /v1/auth/sessions) or GitHub OAuth

RunnerBearerAuth.description: The opaque agt_r token minted when the runner enrols (POST /v1/runners)
